source_text:
6.6
Οτι οὐκ ε στιν ἐν τῷ θανάτῳ ὁ
μνημονεύων σου.
Πᾶς ὁ μνημονεύων τῆς ζωῆς, τῆς εἰπού σης· ̓Εγώ εἰμι ἡ ζωὴ,
οὐκ ε στιν ἐν θανάτῳ.
pass_a_gloss: Because not there-is in the death the one-remembering you. Every the one-remembering of-the Life, of-the having-said: I am the life, not there-is in death.
pass_b_english: “Because there is not in death the one who remembers you” (Psalm 6:6).
Everyone who remembers the Life, who said “I am the life” (John 11:25), is not in death.

choices.term: τῆς ζωῆς, τῆς εἰπούσης· Ἐγώ εἰμι ἡ ζωή
choices.english: the Life, who said I am the life
choices.why: ζωή is personified as Christ speaking John 11:25, not generic vitality.

anf_compare.notes: ANF lacks this Greek catena as reading English.
